title: Binary search
summary: Search in a sorted array by repeatedly halving the search space. Compare target with middle element; if equal, found; if less, search left half; if greater, search right half. O(log n) comparisons. Requires sorted array. Variants: lower_bound (first ≥ target), upper_bound (first > target), binary search on answer (monotonic predicate).

structure.meaning: Each iteration halves the search space.
Find first element ≥ target. Returns insertion point.
Find first element > target. Returns insertion point.
Search for the smallest x such that predicate(x) is true. Requires monotonic predicate.

notes: Binary search is O(log n) comparisons.
Binary search requires a sorted array (or monotonic predicate).
Off-by-one errors are the most common bug (use lo + (hi-lo)/2 to avoid overflow).
Binary search on answer is used for optimization problems (minimize/maximize with monotonic constraint).
Interpolation search achieves O(log log n) for uniformly distributed data.
